fixes.explanation: Strangers sounds soft, but it's not Paul's word. Paul is the apostle writing this letter, and he says they “were slaves” to those who by nature are not gods. A stranger just walks past you, and that's a long way from a slave. Paul picked the heavier word.

That's it. Paul asks, “…how is it that you are turning back to those weak and worthless principles?” Notice the words turning back. They know God now, and I think Paul is stunned they'd go back to those principles.

True. Paul asks, “Do you wish to be enslaved by them all over again?” It's a question, and I think he asks it so they'll stop and look at where they're headed. I bet hearing the word enslaved out loud lands hard.

Not quite, friend. Paul says the opposite: “You have done me no wrong.” That comes right after he begs them, “…become like me, for I became like you.” Right in the middle of his worry, those words stand plain.

Right, it's false. Paul says, “You have done me no wrong.” That comes right after he begs them, “…become like me, for I became like you.” So the Galatians haven't wronged him, and that's straight from Paul.

That's what Paul says. They “…welcomed me as if I were an angel of God…” and he adds, “…as if I were Christ Jesus Himself.” Paul says it was because of an illness that he first preached the gospel to them, and that's how they welcomed him. I think that tells you how warm it was.

A king would get a parade, but Paul doesn't say that. He says they welcomed him “…as if I were an angel of God, as if I were Christ Jesus Himself.” He says his illness was a trial to them, and they still did not despise or reject him.

True. Paul says they welcomed him “…as if I were Christ Jesus Himself.” He says it was because of an illness that he first preached the gospel to them, and they welcomed him like that. It's the kind of welcome I'd have fallen over for after all my years stuck in the back of a junk drawer.
Land is a big thing to give, but it's not on the page. Paul says, “…if it were possible, you would have torn out your eyes and given them to me.” That's about as personal as a gift can get.

Enemy is the word. Paul asks, “Have I now become your enemy by telling you the truth?” It's a question, and I think it stings, since they once welcomed him “…as if I were an angel of God…” That's quite a change to ask about.
Judge is close in feeling, but it's not Paul's word. He asks, “Have I now become your enemy by telling you the truth?” Enemy is a sharper word, and I bet it carries a lot of weight for him.

Right. Paul says, “…they want to isolate you from us, so that you may be zealous for them.” They want the Galatians cut off from “us,” and the goal is that the Galatians be zealous for them. It's like someone moving you to a quiet table so only they can talk to you.
Nothing about rulers is in these verses. Paul says those people “…want to isolate you from us, so that you may be zealous for them.” It's about isolating the Galatians from “us,” as Paul puts it.

True. Paul says they want to isolate the Galatians “…so that you may be zealous for them.” Their goal, in Paul's words, is that the Galatians be zealous for them. I think Paul sees it clearly, and he wants the Galatians to see it too.
It's true, and Paul says it plainly. Those people want to isolate the Galatians from “us,” “…so that you may be zealous for them.” He's pointing out where their zeal is aimed.

Yes. Paul says it's good to be zealous for a noble purpose, “…at any time, and not only when I am with you.” In other words, that zeal isn't meant to depend on him being there. It's the same zeal whether Paul is around or not.

His tone, yes. Paul says, “…how I wish I could be with you now and change my tone, because I am perplexed about you.” I think a letter is hard because you can't see a face while you say a hard thing. Being there with them is how he wishes he could change it.
Travel plans don't come up. Paul does wish he could be with them, but what he says he'd change is “…my tone, because I am perplexed about you.” He names a tone, not a trip.
Message isn't the word Paul uses. He says he wishes he could be with them and “…change my tone…” Tone is the one thing he names, and he doesn't mention changing anything else.
